instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Meanwhile, chop the onion, dice the bell pepper and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Shred the cheese. That should be about 2 cups.

Heat the 1 tbsp oil in a large oven safe skillet, about 10 inches, over medium high. Add the 1 lb beef and the 1/4 tsp salt and break it up with a spoon. Leave it alone for 3 minutes so the bottom browns, then stir and cook for 3 minutes, until there's no pink left.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft. Spoon off any fat pooling in the pan.
Add the garlic and the 2 tbsp taco seasoning and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Stir in 1/4 cup water and let it bubble for 2 minutes, until it's almost gone. Stir in 3/4 cup of the enchilada sauce and take the pan off the heat.
Taste the filling. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Smooth the filling flat and scatter 1 1/2 cups of the cheese over it. If you don't have an oven safe skillet, transfer the filling to a 2 quart baking dish first.
In a bowl, stir together the corn muffin mix, the 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup of the frozen corn, the 1/3 cup milk and the egg, until there are no dry streaks. It'll be thick.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter over the filling and spread it gently to the edges. Scatter the remaining 1/2 cup cheese on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the top is golden and a toothpick in the center of the cornbread comes out clean. If the top browns before then, lay a piece of foil loosely over it.
Let it sit for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, chop a handful of the cilantro.
Scatter the cilantro over the top and serve with the rest of the sour cream.
method_notes: Both brown ground beef with onion, bell pepper and garlic, season it with taco seasoning, loosen it with a tomato or enchilada sauce, cover it with cheese and bake a corn muffin batter over the top. Spend With Pennies, the lead, uses 1 lb of beef with 3/4 cup enchilada sauce and a single box of corn muffin mix stirred with sour cream, corn, milk and an egg, baked at 350°F for 35 to 40 minutes, and says it can go in one ovenproof skillet. Melissa's Southern Style Kitchen doubles it for a 9x13 pan with Rotel tomatoes, Colby Jack and a buttermilk cornbread with green chiles, baked at 375°F for 30 minutes. This follows the lead for one skillet and four hearty portions, blooms the seasoning in the pan before the liquid goes in, and puts the rest of the sour cream on the table.
